steps.prompt: Two parallel lines are crossed by a third line, making eight angles. If you know just one of them, how many of the other seven can you find?

cards.title: The angle facts
cards.body: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$, and around a point to $360^\circ$. Vertical (opposite) angles are equal. The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$, and an exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles not next to it. The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

cards.title: Worked example: a ratio of angles
cards.problem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 4$. What is the largest angle?

steps.text: There are $2 + 3 + 4 = 9$ equal parts in $180^\circ$, so one part is $20^\circ$.

try.prompt: How many degrees is one part?
What is the largest angle, in degrees?

cards.title: Parallel lines and chasing
cards.body: When a line crosses two parallel lines, corresponding angles and alternate angles are equal, and co-interior angles (between the lines, on the same side) add to $180^\circ$. Angle chasing: write every angle you find on the figure, call an unknown $x$, and keep going until you reach the one you want.

cards.title: Worked example: an isosceles triangle
cards.problem: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of $40^\circ$. Find a base angle, then the exterior angle at that base corner.

steps.text: The base angles share $180 - 40 = 140$, so each is $70^\circ$.

try.prompt: What is each base angle, in degrees?

steps.text: The exterior angle is $180 - 70 = 110^\circ$, which is also $40 + 70$.

try.prompt: What is the exterior angle at a base corner?

cards.title: The common trap: trusting the picture
cards.body: AMC figures are not drawn to scale unless they say so. Don't assume lines are parallel, angles are right or sides are equal because they look it: use only what you are told. And the exterior angle is the sum of the two FAR interior angles, not the one next to it.

prompts: Which angle fact do you use most when you chase angles?
